title: What is the secret prompt you use when developing games with AI?
author: TheHeistGameSupport
selftext: When I use it, I just give instructions; I don't use any specific prompts. If you know of any that work well, could you share them?

comments.author: TheMarco
comments.body: Just instructions. I'm not aware of any "magic prompts". I typically start with a very simple gameplay proof of concept. Then I play it and ask myself: "Is this actually fun to play?" and if so I start fleshing it out.

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
"What are the secret brushstrokes you use as an artist to paint a painting?" 

Shaping the prompts are itself the skill. Someone telling you what brushstrokes they used won't help you create a beautiful painting. You want technique, not prompts.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Separate design from implementation.

Instead of "make the game", first "make the design; don't code anything". We discuss the design for a while. And the make the game according to the design. You get better results.

comments.author: gholias
comments.body:
Not a prompt, but the more I build, the more examples I have to feed the agent to avoid errors.

“Create the animations. Use the project at projects/old-project as an example for spritesheet animation”

“Add the sound effects. Use the same implementation as my other project”

This way each project/tests becomes the stepping stone for the next one.

If you don’t have multiple projects, try to build multiple small focused prototypes 

Instead of “build me a game like Diablo 2”

Try   
“Build me an isometric character sprite”  
“Build me the controls to move it around”  
“Build the system to control hp and mana”  
“Build an attack button”  
“Build an enemy”  
“Now put all the tests we did together so I can control the char and attack the enemy”

This is how I normally work to have better control of the quality of the output

replies.author: gholias
replies.body:
yes, make a plan to implement the game. You can do that with a brainstorm session with an AI model. Something like this:

Prompt 1 - GDD  
"I want to create a game like Tetris, but instead of blocks I want to have squishes in shaped like a butter bar.

Help me brainstorm the game GDD (Game Design Document). My goal is to have a game that can be played in a website"

Prompt 2 - Plan  
"Read the GDD at /file/location.md and create a mult-phased plan to implement the game. After each Phase, I want to have a delivarable that I can test and validate before we move to the next phase. Quality is very important, so break the phases in a way we build the game building blocks in the quality and refinament that I expect from the final product"

Prompt 3 - Execute  
"Implement phase 0"

Prompt 4 - Validate and Interate  
"I did not like how the squish is being animated. Lets reword that"

or  
"Phase 0 is completed, lets start phase 1"

do that until the game is complete and with the quality you expect

comments.author: Funnyman1217
comments.body:
Plan, document, build

Start in plan mode and work back and forth with your harness to plan out the game you want built.   
Have the harness build a complete set of documents outlining the project of building the game. This includes skills, mcps and integrations with tools you plan to use alongside ai or have AI use.   
Once you have a complete project plan and the harness is ready to build have it work through each phase of the project and have you do player testing through out. 

I have been doing ai development since before tool calling was a thing and system prompt was the only prompt feed to an LLM. 

I dont find and use prompts for my AI. I tell my harness to build the prompts and skills needed for each task and have the project document set them as requirements. Id rather it understand the prompt then me.

comments.author: EffectNo2152
comments.body:
show this to your ai

I started with normal AI coding chats.  
Then I connected the AI to my actual dev PC.  
Now I can do a surprising amount of game development from my phone while the PC does the heavy lifting.  
Phone = control panel  
AI = planner/operator  
PC = dev machine  
Blender = asset factory  
Vite = live testing  
GitHub = source control + automation  
itch.io = deployment  
Main tools:  
ChatGPT / coding models  
Plans features, writes code, debugs, and coordinates the workflow.  
ECC / Hermes Agent  
Agent harness/orchestration stuff. Helps turn “write code” into a more structured plan, build, test, review, fix loop.  
Desktop Commander  
Lets the AI actually use my Windows PC: terminal, files, Git, scripts, servers, Blender jobs, etc.  
Vite + HMR  
Runs the game locally and updates changes almost instantly.  
LAN / Tailscale  
Lets me open the local build on my phone and test the real mobile version.  
Blender + Blender Python  
AI can generate or edit 3D geometry, materials, scenes, renders, and exports with scripts.  
Blender MCP / MCP  
Lets AI agents call external tools through a standardized tool interface.  
Asset Forge  
My own pipeline for:  
request  
research  
plan  
Blender build  
materials  
QA  
export  
reusable asset library  
The important part is reuse.  
If it makes a good material, tree, road, building module, decal, etc., keep it.  
The 100th asset should be easier to make than the 1st.  
OpenStreetMap + USGS  
Real roads, buildings, terrain, and elevation data for making game maps based on real places.  
Three.js / Godot  
The game/runtime side depending on the project.  
Python + Node/npm  
Automation glue.  
ElevenLabs  
Voices, dialogue, announcers, fake radio hosts, commercials, etc.  
Kokoro / local TTS  
Cheap/local speech generation for larger batches.  
Suno  
Music experiments.  
Git + GitHub  
Version control, branches, backups, source of truth.  
GitHub Actions + Butler  
Automated builds and deployment to itch.io.  
So the loop is basically:  
I type something on my phone.  
AI plans it.  
AI controls the dev PC.  
It edits code, runs Blender, or generates assets.  
Vite updates the game.  
I test it on my phone.  
I say “this is broken.”  
AI fixes it.  
Git saves the working version.  
GitHub stores it.  
The build gets deployed to itch.io.  
The big realization for me was that the interesting part isn’t just “AI writes code.”  
It’s giving the AI tools and feedback loops.  
Plan.  
Build.  
Test.  
Break something.  
Fix it.  
Test again.  
Save it.  
Ship it.  
If somebody wanted to copy the simplest version of this, I’d start with:  
AI + remote PC access + Git + Vite + Blender  
Then add the rest later.  
I’m still a noob at a lot of the individual pieces.  
I basically just kept connecting stuff together until my desktop turned into the studio and my phone turned into mission control.

comments.author: Substantial_Fish6717
comments.body: There isn't a secret prompt. What you need to do is give it a reference to works towards, if it's an existing art or an existing game, or even a concept art that you generated with chatgpt. Then you give it the reference and you ask to work towards meeting that reference. And don't stop until you ask it to stop or it matches the look exactly. Also, you need to have a Lead, blind critics, an art director and an adversary reviewer. You will waste a lot of tokens, but eventually you will get there.
